articles.title: Strongest group I have ever had - Barnet boss Brennan
articles.summary: Barnet boss Dean Brennan says his squad is the "strongest" he's ever worked with, after their 2-1 win over Accrington.
articles.body:
Barnet boss Dean Brennan says the strength in depth in his squad was underlined by their 2-1 win over Accrington on Saturday - and an ultra-competitive 11-a-side game in training in the build-up.

Brennan says his players "could have sulked" after conceding an injury-time equaliser in a 3-3 draw at Chesterfield last week, but, instead, those who had not been featuring took their chance to impress during the week.

"At Chesterfield, we come away feeling aggrieved that we didn't win the game. We definitely should have won it by two clear goals," Brennan told BBC Radio London.

"We could have sulked but I watched the players train on Tuesday. We played an 11-a-side game and I said to them 'you've got to play like this is your last game at Barnet'.

"The lads that hadn't been playing won 5-2 against the first team and it was a fantastic game. I was going to change the team [against Accrington] but I thought we were that good at Chesterfield, I'll keep the same team."

But Brennan admitted that he had to make a tactical tweak at half-time after going 1-0 behind, and two Charlie Lakin goals turned it around.

"We had a sacrificial lamb in Nnamdi Ofoborh , who had to come off," Brennan said. "Then we put Damola [Ajayi] out on the right-hand side, and he gave us width.

"Once you have the ammunition like that and you make the right subs, it's always a good feeling to win. And Lakin's been sensational, hasn't he? What a signing he's been.

"This is the strongest group of players I've ever had."

Among the thousands at one of Harry Styles ' recent Madison Square Garden (MSG) shows was New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson , who was having a night out with his wife, Ali.

"Madison Square Garden, home of the world champion New York Knicks . We may or may not have the King of New York in the house tonight… Mr. Jalen Brunson ," he said, saluting the captain.

After the crowd showered Brunson with a lengthy round of applause, the pop star slyly said, "He's just trying to have a quiet night out — not a chance. Not in this city. It's like Mickey Mouse going to Disneyland."

Within the blink of an eye, Styles is almost a third of the way through his 30-night residency at Madison Square Garden. He will continue performing shows on his Together, Together Tour at MSG through Oct. 31. This marks the second tour in a row with a show on Halloween at the Garden.

Styles recently announced a slew of new dates for 2027. He will perform 25 more shows across 12 cities. Most of the cities are new for the tour, but he will return for three more shows at Wembley Stadium from Aug. 25 to 28.

Brunson, meanwhile, is no stranger to MSG. He is one of the few who work at the Garden more than Styles as part of the Knicks. Over the last few months, Brunson has become the King of New York, thanks to the Knicks' championship win.

He was crucial in bringing the Knicks their first championship in 53 years. Brunson was named NBA Finals MVP for his performance in the series, averaging 32.6 points per game. His 45-point masterclass in Game 5 put the San Antonio Spurs away.

articles.title: Niko Kovac calls them ‘finishers’
articles.summary: With the score at 1:0 in the home game against the newly promoted side, Kovac brought on Felix Nmecha, Marcel Sabitzer and Carney Chukwuemeka after just over...
articles.body:
With the score at 1:0 in the home game against the newly promoted side, Kovac brought on Felix Nmecha , Marcel Sabitzer and Carney Chukwuemeka after just over an hour; Maximilian Beier and Ramy Bensebaini followed a little under 15 minutes before the end.

Fabio Silva had already scored the 1:2 as a substitute in the Super Cup against FC Bayern Munich , and last weekend the Portuguese forward came off the bench to make it 2:2 at TSG Hoffenheim before Ethan Nwaneri , also a substitute in that match, forced the own goal for the 3:2 winner. In midweek, Serhou Guirassy benefited from an assist by the substituted-in Silva for his goal to make it 2:1 against Villarreal CF (final score 3:2). And now Paderborn: two goals from super-sub Nmecha, plus a shot off the crossbar from Sabitzer.

Niko Kovac calls them "finishers." The ones who come on "can steer games in the right direction. And we already have quite a few of them," says the head coach.

Already in the previous 2025/26 Bundesliga season, only Bayern Munich's substitutes (20) scored more often than Borussia Dortmund 's (19).

"We need a squad with quality, breadth and depth," Kovac stresses, repeatedly showing how to influence games successfully with his decisions. But he does not talk about himself, instead emphasizing: "We have a lot more people than just eleven – and I'm very happy about that."

The fact that so much quality is sitting on the bench also has pragmatic reasons, "because we have a lot of games and also many internationals. We have to rotate in consultation with our medical department; other clubs do the same." Another important side effect: "Competition keeps you sharp. The battle for places is there this season too. If you have no competition, you sit back, you take it easy, you become sluggish, and then you don't get the results you want..."

At the moment, everything fits: rotation, competition for places and impact from the bench in six of BVB's 12 goals (excluding the cup game against a fifth-division side), all involving substitutes. Boris Rupert

The Boston Bruins ( prospects ) are back on the ice.

The Bruins and Sabres opened the Prospects Showcase yesterday in Buffalo . The Bruins jumped out to a lead immediately and got contributions from five different goal scorers, while Max Lundgren stopped all but two.

Elsewhere around the league, the NHL is continuing its top 50 players right now list. There is more on Adam Fantilli , who is still unsigned in Columbus. The Canadiens signed a 23-year-old to a four-year deal, and the Blue Jackets handed out a PTO.

There's also more from other prospect games going on in the NHL.

Happy Monday, catch up on Bruins and league news in today's Daily Bean :

PROSPECTS SHOWCASE : The Bruins are back… kind of. The prospects took to the ice for the first game of the Prospects Showcase. Attilio Biasca got the scoring started 25 seconds in, and he was one of five goal scorers for the black and gold yesterday. James Hagens ? He centered the first line and scored twice.

The two Sabres goals were on the power play.

The Bruins are back on the ice today at noon for Game 2 .

NHL.com : The NHL Network's top 50 players right now list continues to roll out. Yesterday, Nos. 30-21 were revealed, and five of the players play in the Atlantic Division.

NHLTradeRumors.me : Adam Fantilli is still unsigned. He has not been at Blue Jackets' team events ahead of training camp, and with a few days to go before camp starts, there has not been much progress in extension talks. Danny Briere changed the market when he handed Leo Carlsson an offer sheet with an $18M AAV, and that's directly impacting the Fantilli negotiations.

The Blue Jackets have $12,645,001 in cap space.

Montreal Hockey Now : The Montreal Canadiens signed forward Zachary Bolduc to a 4x$4.2M extension yesterday. The 23-year-old did not have a contract going into this season, and his usage gets a little more complicated after the Chris Kreider signing. Marc Dumont has the instant analysis on yesterday's signing.

Sportsnet : The Canadiens are making an easy bet on Chris Kreider 's experience and offensive upside. Kreider left bigger deals on the table to land in Montreal, according to his agent, but the fit and comfort level played a factor.

Pittsburgh Hockey Now : The Penguins went from the tournament in Buffalo to a tournament in Detroit . articles.title: Eagles News: Jalen Hurts starts the season strong
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 9/14/26.
articles.body:
Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

Jalen Hurts looking good was my biggest takeaway from the Eagles' Week 1 win. The offense as a whole was … uneven … but QB1 made big plays to carry the team to victory. His run to pick up a first down on 3rd-and-18 was massive and he made some really nice precision throws (see: Dallas Goedert 's first touchdown, DeVonta Smith 's sideline catch). The offense has a lot to clean up and improve upon … but it's always easier to feel good about your favorite team's outlook when the QB is playing well.

Let's get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

Considering the pocket was breaking down snap after snap, Hurts was terrific Sunday. On the Eagles' third possession, he heaved a perfect 64-yard bomb down the right sideline to the 6-yard-line to newcomer Dontayvion Wicks and after Cam Jurgens ' second penalty of the quarter, threw a dart to Dallas Goedert in the end zone for a 17-yard touchdown. Two spectacular throws on his sixth and seventh passes ever in Sean Mannion's offense. Encouraging start. Later in the second quarter a terrific nine-yard TD pass to Wicks, and with six minutes left in the fourth quarter he found Goedert open over the middle and lobbed him a short pass that the veteran tight end turned into a 43-yard touchdown, longest by an Eagles tight end since Brent Celek 's 65-yarder in the historic comeback win at the Meadowlands in 2010. Considering how little help he was getting up front, I thought Hurts was outstanding in his first game working with Mannion. He also had some terrific runs – a 14-yarder on a 1st-and-20 in the third quarter and a 22-yarder on a 3rd-and-18 on the 4th-quarter TD drive. When he ran it was out of desperation under duress not out of any kind of set play. Hurts finished 14-for-25 for 203 yards with the three TD passes and no interceptions and a 122.2 passer rating along with 48 rushing yards on five runs before a couple kneel downs. He overcame a lot.

Jalen Hurts let out a chuckle and a smile while he contemplated what he would say, and perhaps more tellingly, what he wouldn't. The Eagles quarterback was asked about his first touchdown pass of the new season and the fact that it looked eerily similar to the final play of the season before. Hurts found Dallas Goedert running up the seam on the same four vertical route concept that had become the lasting symbol for the group's offensive struggles in 2025 and the limited menu some blamed the 28-year-old signal caller for during the offseason. So what was going through Hurts' mind after he ripped the throw high enough and far enough into the back of the end zone for only Goedert to make the play and promptly turned toward the sideline, shrugging his shoulders in celebration? "It's a great play. It's a great play," Hurts said with a chuckle. "Y'all will dig. Y'all will try to figure something out."

Jalen Hurts' first game under Sean Mannion is in the books, as the Eagles held tough against a feisty Commanders team thanks to Dallas Goedert's two touchdowns, a big day for Tay Wicks and characteristic tough defense from Zack Baun , Nolan Smith and crew. Two-time Super Bowl champion and future Eagles Hall of Famer Brandon Graham joins the show, along with Brandon Lee Gowton and Bo Wulf, plus insight from Fran Duffy, Miles Johnston and EJ Smith, live from the LINC.

Did the Eagles' new offense pass the test Week 1? There was a boom-or-bust element to it, but the explosive plays carried them to a passing grade and a win over Washington. From WR Dontayvion Wicks' 64-yard reception (a career high) to QB Jalen Hurts' 22-yard scramble on third-and-18 to TE Dallas Goedert's 43-yard score moments later, there was plenty to be encouraged about from offensive coordinator Sean Mannion's debut. Some issues along the offensive front (left guard Landon Dickerson looked as if he was laboring) and long stretches of ineffectiveness brought back memories of 2025, but patience is required while Philly breaks in a new system. What to make of the QB performance: Hurts threw three touchdowns, was timely with his runs and didn't commit a turnover. The pass-and-catch between the signal-caller and new WR1 DeVonta Smith along the right sideline late in the third quarter was a thing of beauty. Hurts was at his best when attacking downfield, completing 6 of 9 such attempts for 176 yards.

Let's see it through midnight green glasses: The Eagles won. Jalen Hurts took snaps under center. He threw down the middle of the field. The Eagles just happened to be playing against two new coordinators and a Wahington Commanders team that had to do more learning on the job than the Eagles did. The Eagles survived a 24-22 scare over Washington on Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field to keep Eagles' head coach Nick Sirianni a perfect 6-0 in season opening games and 35-14 overall. Under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, Hurts completed 14 of 25 for 203 yards and three touchdowns—two TDs down the middle of the field on third down. Hurts rushed for 46 yards and made some strong throws. His 22-yard scramble in the fourth quarter saved the game. He made sure nine different Eagles touched the ball. Hurts prides himself on finding ways to win—and it is what he did.

10) The 'Thank You' Award 🙏: The schedule makers. If the Eagles had played a better team, maybe this would have been a loss? We'll never know. The Eagles will get another soft opponent Week 2 to work out the kinks when they travel to Nashville to take on the Tennessee Titans , who lost decisively to the lowly Jets Week 1.

Neither team played well. The Eagles just made more winning plays and that proved to be the difference in the game. The Eagles have plenty of issues to work on. The OL was very up and down. Landon Dickerson really struggled. He allowed a sack, a TFL and was called for at least one penalty. Cam Jurgens drew a couple of flags. Jordan Mailata had one. They struggled to consistently block the WAS front on run plays.

Eagles use big plays to outlast Commanders. Much like the last several seasons, the Eagles offense wasn't pretty, but it got the job done, eking out a two-point win over a division rival. Philly's offense was an inconsistent mess for much of the day, with the offensive line struggling to pick up the new blocking scheme, allowing far too many free runners into the backfield. However, Nick Sirianni's club used a trove of big plays that made the difference. Saquon Barkley had a 42-yard scamper that helped set up a second-quarter score. Jalen Hurts, who was up-and-down, splashed three passes that went at least 30 yards, including the difference-making 43-yard catch-and-run TD from Dallas Goedert. The big plays covered for an offense that went three-and-out four times, including three straight to start the second half. There are obvious kinks to iron out with Sean Mannion's system, but a win's a win.

How about Zack Baun? He is off to an All-Pro start – 12 total tackles, two passes defensed, one tackle for loss. Just a great football player. The entire defensive line won with power, speed, and discipline. Jihaad Campbell had the lone quarterback sack – a play started by Ojomo – and nine total tackles. The Eagles gave up some plays in the fourth quarter but, hey, that is something to correct. Overall, a lot more good things than not, led by Baun. "Happy to get a win, especially in a division game," Baun said. "Those games are crucial down the stretch and you never know what position you're going to be at the end of the season and to get one at the beginning is nice."

Former Eagles QB with a nice game against former Eagles defensive coordinator and current Packers DC Jonathan Gannon.

Stock Up — Carson Wentz . Wentz showed his limitations, and as he said after the game it's better to be lucky than good when it came to penalties erasing a redzone interception, but he also showed he could move the offense under difficult circumstances with few reps in practice. He finished 12/19 for 133 yards and 3 TDs and a 123.5 passer rating.

Christian Parker was afforded an enormous amount of optimism and trust over the offseason. To be clear, he could still wind up being the answer. One game does not make anything. But the first outing for this new-look defense felt a lot like all of them for the group that they are trying to replace, one of the worst defenses in franchise history. Unfortunately it felt like more of the same, the same failing grades where the bare minimum of passing felt so far out of reach. Maybe Parker and company will turn things around over their version of summer school? The analogy is difficult to build on at this point because nobody expected this. Nobody expected more of the same. How did this possibly happen?

Daniels had to make a quick judgement call in the moment, and he followed his rules on that play by choosing to shovel the ball inside. Quinn and Daniels stood by the call, which will be negatively viewed because of the result. "The 2-point play, we just didn't execute," Daniels said. "It was the right call. Anything Blough calls, I'm with him. Regardless of who everyone else might view it, I'm with Blough 100%."

Jaxson Dart — The second-year quarterback was outstanding against the Cowboys. He completed 23 of 29 passes (79.3%), for 230 yards, and three touchdowns. He ran 11 times for 54 yards. He got down or out of bounds when he needed to. He made big throws when the Giants needed them. He played the way a franchise quarterback is supposed to play.

The NFL is wrapping up Week 1, but the first odds of Week 2 have arrived at FanDuel Sportsbook. All 16 games have odds at this point, but with SNF and MNF still to play, we can expect some movement in the next 36 hours. Week 2 kicks off with the Bills hosting the Lions. Buffalo won a wild one, scoring a touchdown after the two-minute warning to secure a 36-31 win over the Texans . Detroit had to go to overtime and barely hold off a game Saints squad. After the Lions scored a touchdown in overtime, New Orleans advanced down the field and matched the TD. They went for two and the win but came up short after strong Lions coverage. The Sunday slate includes some fun ones in Week 2. Bengals-Texans and Jaguars-Broncos will be interesting. Saints-Ravens is suddenly an interesting one in its own right. The 49ers are the biggest favorite nex tweek, laying nearly two touchdowns against the Dolphins.

articles.title: 3 things we learned from the Bengals’ Week 1 win over the Bucs
articles.summary: Cincinnati’s bend-but-don’t-break defense can actually help them win games.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals held on for a 33-27 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

After a long offseason of conjecture, we finally know what the defense can actually do.

Yes, they're still a little leaky, missing tackles. And they were flagged for being line up offsides multiple times. But they're bold and chomping at the bit to make a big play.

It's somewhat similar to those playmaking defenses in 2021 and 2022. Bend but don't break, with some turnovers in between that give the offense a nice boost.

The four fumbles and four sacks were a lot more than we would've seen out of the defenses in 2024 and 2025, and three early fumble recoveries are what gave the Bengals a nice cushion for the game.

It's not an injury thing; Joe Burrow just needs real reps to warm up

For a QB with as high of a football IQ as Joe Burrow, his interception was a head scratcher.

The only real explanation is that Burrow just needs some time to get back into a rhythm in the regular season.

It kinda makes sense when you consider how little the seventh-year QB has played in the preseason.

The good news is, he was able to do just enough to secure a victory in Week 1, so the offense should only be better from here on out.

Touches on offense are going to be more evenly distributed

With Ja'Marr Chase being the focus of the Bucs' secondary and only getting four targets, Burrow looked elsewhere.

Chase Brown had six targets, which was as many as Tee Higgins. But it was Mike Gesicki who led the team with seven targets. Drew Sample, Andrei Iosivas, and Samaje Perine had three targets, and Dohnte Meyers and Tanner Hudson even got a look each.

And the run-to-pass ratio was solid, with 27 runs and 35 passes.

There has been talk of a move to a more traditional approach on offense with Dan Pitcher more involved in play design, but now it seems to be official.

articles.title: Man Utd fans' ownership protests intensify
articles.summary: To be clear, Manchester United's fans have - to a greater or lesser degree - protested against the owners since the Glazer family landed £600m-worth of debt...
articles.body:
To be clear, Manchester United 's fans have - to a greater or lesser degree - protested against the owners since the Glazer family landed £600m-worth of debt on to a previously debt-free club with their leveraged buy-out in 2005.

In their most recent accounts to 31 March, United had an overall debt of £1.3bn, including outstanding transfer fees.

Since then they have refinanced $425m (£314m) worth of bonds at a higher interest rate than they had been previously. They also took an additional $125m (£92.4m) but are yet to explain what the additional funds will be used for.

The club's current financial position will be revealed on 23 September when it publishes its full year accounts to 30 June 2026.

Ratcliffe's involvement promised to change the situation. Yet many fans argue that, if anything, things have got worse.

Ill feeling has spilled over since United launched a ticket-touting investigation in the summer.

Although they have admitted to underestimating the number of fans who shared their account details and toned down some of the threats around season ticket confiscation if supporters failed to respond as requested, United officials defended the investigation.

Last week, they revealed 685 fan accounts had been banned, with a further 464 either sanctioned or warned.

However, United added that "468 cases were resolved after supporters responded with the relevant information. No further action was taken, as the information provided satisfactorily explained the activity identified".

Huge numbers with flares gathered outside the ground, heeding a call from the 1958 Group, before making their way through the Munich tunnel under the stadium.

It was noticeable many songs were sung in direct protest against Ratcliffe, as well as the Glazers.

"We wanted the Glazers out and that will never change," said Steve Compton of the the 1958 Group.

"Ratcliffe came in and gave us a glimmer, but his idea of putting Manchester back in Man Utd couldn't be any further from the truth.

There were boos from the home fans at the final whistle, although it was not entirely clear whether the reaction was triggered by their team's performance or the officials over the controversial offside call that confirmed Erling Haaland 's second-half winner should stand.

Since Berrada spoke to staff, United have delivered their worst starts in three decades. Many United supporters feel an overall transfer spend of £148m this summer was not enough after Carrick's mid-season arrival led to an improvement that secured a third-place finish.

"I definitely appreciate the supporters," said Carrick.

"We want to try everything to make them happy. They're everything for this football club. I never take them for granted. I speak about that quite a lot, and it means a lot to me.

"I'm feeling for them today on the back of losing the game. We haven't got as many points as we would have liked at this point, for sure. There's no getting away from that."

articles.title: Ravens Report Card, Week 1: Encouraging start to the season as Ravens dominate all three phases
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens began the 2026 season with a bang in Week 1, scoring 41 points en route to a 21-point victory over the Indianapolis Colts. While it was...
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens began the 2026 season with a bang in Week 1, scoring 41 points en route to a 21-point victory over the Indianapolis Colts . While it was not a flawless performance, the Ravens never trailed after the first few minutes of the game and quickly opened up a three-possession lead, which they never relinquished.

Let's break down how every position group fared in this week's report card.

Lamar Jackson had a strong performance to begin the season, completing 17-of-25 passes for 324 yards and a touchdown — with another 40 rushing yards and a score on the ground. Jackson connected with Zay Flowers for multiple chunk plays through the air and delivered another long 50+ yard pass in the third quarter. Jackson looked to be command of Declan Doyle's offense and he's clearly no longer compromised by injuries athletically. The lone blemish of Jackson's day was a lost fumble where he was strip sacked in the Ravens' own territory, which led to a Colts' touchdown. Jackson was sacked almost immediately after turning around in play action, though, and fortunately the Ravens were up by three scores at the time, so it wasn't a damaging sequence.

It was just another day at the office for Derrick Henry in Week 1, who rushed for 144 yards on 24 carries with three touchdowns. Henry also added 19 receiving yards on a good catch-and-run reception. Henry's longest run on the day went for 32 yards, and he grinded out chunk gains as the game progressed to help keep the Ravens' offense on the field and put the game away. Justice Hill had 28 scrimmage yards on seven touches behind him, picking up a nice first-down gain through the air.

Before exiting with a hamstring injury before halftime, Flowers had already set a new career-high in receiving yards with 150 on five catches. He had a long 54-yard touchdown catch and fell just a few yards short of scoring on the second drive of the game. Flowers was uncoverable and had he left the game early, there's no telling what his final stat line may have been. His performance alone in just two quarters of action is enough to boost this position group's grade. Chris Moore , who was a practice squad elevation, made an impact with a 54-yard reception in the third quarter. LaJohntay Wester had two catches, and Ja'Kobi Lane had one 11-yard catch before leaving the game early as well with a wrist injury. Lane would have had his first career touchdown reception, but it was called back due to a holding penalty. Surprisingly, Rashod Bateman was held to zero catches on just one target.

Mark Andrews ' first target resulted in a dropped pass, and he was also flagged for a false start in the red zone early in the game. That was a discouraging start, but he wound up reeling in four receptions for 49 yards overall. His six targets were tied with Flowers for most on the team. Matthew Hibner turned a short out-route pass into a 13-yard gain to help push the Ravens deeper into the red zone, setting up a score. Hibner wasn't targeted again in the game, and rookie Josh Cuevas was not a factor in the passing game. Veteran Durham Smythe caught one pass for a short four-yard gain outside of the end zone. The Ravens' tight ends as a whole seemed to do a good job of pass blocking and holding the edges in run blocking situations.

It was not the most encouraging start to the season for the Ravens' new-look offensive line. While they did a good job in run blocking and held up okay for most of the game in pass protection, the penalties from this group were rough. Of the Ravens' 10 penalties overall as a team, most of them were offensive line pre-snap calls, holding violations and in one instance a chop-blocking flag. It seemed like the Ravens were flagged for offensive line penalties on almost every drive and many times it negated a first-down gain or score. There were some instances where the Colts generated quick pressure up the middle, too, and they did get home on Jackson to force a fumble in the second quarter.

Travis Jones was a force up front in this game with two notable tackles for loss, one of which he drove Taylor back several yards behind the line of scrimmage. Taylor was able to find running room against the Ravens' defensive front a number of times, though, and the Ravens allowed 102 rushing yards overall and 5.2 yards per carry. Broderick Washington had a nice pass breakup early in the game that was close to being an interception, and Aaenas Peebles had a quarterback hit as well.

Trey Hendrickson 's debut did not result in any splash plays, but he was close to getting home for a sack or possible forced fumble multiple times. Hendrickson had a handful of pressures on Jones and his presence may have helped opened things up a bit for Tavius Robinson , who had a big showing on the opposite side of the defensive front. Robinson racked up four quarterback hits with a sack and tackle for loss. In a contract year, this could be the start of a career-best season for the fourth-year edge rusher. Mike Green and Zion Young did not find their way onto the box score in this game.

Roquan Smith 's interception on the Colts' second drive of the game was a thing of beauty, as he deceived Daniel Jones and tapped the ball to himself in the air before securing it. The Ravens added another touchdown a few plays later to open up an eight-point lead. Smith led the team in tackles with 11 and also had a quarterback hit. Next to him, Trenton Simpson had two tackles-for-loss, which was tied for the most of any defender.

Marlon Humphrey had a starring performance with a forced fumble on Jonathan Taylor and third-down knockdown in coverage against Alec Pierce . Humphrey looked much more like his prime self than he did last season, which is an encouraging sign for this season. Nate Wiggins also an impressive pass breakup lined up against Pierce. Keyon Martin made a strong tackle in space against a much larger wide receiver. Overall, the Ravens' corners did a good job limiting big plays in the passing game and were aggressive in coverage.

Following the defense's first drive of the game, Kyle Hamilton began being used more as an extra pass rusher and his presence around the line of scrimmage made a noticeable impact. Hamilton finished with five tackles and a quarterback hit. Malaki Starks was victimized a few times against Taylor via a stiff arm and juke move, but also filled the stat sheet with seven tackles, a sack, two quarterback hits and one tackle for loss. Jaylinn Hawkins didn't make any noticeable impact plays, but he appeared around the ball a few times on some positive defensive plays. The Ravens' three safeties didn't seem to leave the field very much at all.

Tyler Loop answered the bell in a big way, nailing a career-high 57-yard field goal attempt to close out the first half. That expanded the Ravens lead to three possessions, and he made a 45-yarder later in the second half, while also going perfect on all five extra points. Rookie punter Ryan Eckley's three punts went for 140 yards, and Chris Moore had a couple long kick returns to set the Ravens up in good field position offensively. LaJohntay Wester also had a long 30-yard return on a kickoff as well and averaged 10.0 yards per punt return on three tries.

The Tennessee Titans began the Robert Saleh era on a sour note, losing to his former New York Jets team 23-10 at home. The loss continued their season-opening losing streak to six games, with their last win coming at the Denver Broncos in 2020.

articles.title: Knee-jerk reactions after Ravens' impressive offensive showing vs. Colts
articles.summary: It's early, but after a solid performance, this Ravens offense has everyone thinking.
articles.body:
One Baltimore Ravens game certainly won't define a season. Every NFL fan knows that. Coaches preach it. Players repeat it. The smartest observers usually avoid sweeping conclusions after Week 1. That said, sometimes a performance leaves an impression that is hard to ignore. The Ravens looked every bit like a contender during Sunday's 41-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts . The offense rolled up more than 500 yards. Lamar Jackson looked comfortable. Derrick Henry looked unstoppable.

The new coaching staff and its team passed its first test with flying colors . It's still early, but here are a few gut feelings and knee-jerk reactions after Baltimore's season-opening victory.

Derrick Henry can land somewhere between 1,700 and 1,800 rushing yards

After rushing for roughly 150 yards and three touchdowns in the opener, it's difficult not to dream big. Let's be conservative and say Henry averages 100 rushing yards per game the rest of the way. That pace would put him around 1,750 yards for the season. By his standards, that's hardly an outrageous projection.

There will be tougher matchups ahead, and there will undoubtedly be afternoons when defenses slow him down. There will also be games where he completely takes over. Sunday's performance felt like a reminder that Henry remains one of the most dominant runners of his generation.

Lamar Jackson can be an MVP finalist again

That was quite a statement from Baltimore's franchise quarterback. Jackson completed 17 of 25 passes for 324 yards and a touchdown while adding 40 rushing yards and another score on the ground. He looked decisive, explosive, and fully in control of the offense.

It's also worth noting that both of his MVP seasons came while working with a new offensive coordinator. Everything we've heard about Declan Doyle suggests he understands how to maximize Jackson's strengths. If Sunday's performance is a preview of what's ahead, another MVP conversation could be waiting .

Is Declan Doyle flirting with a one-and-done season?

Every year, NFL teams search for the next offensive mastermind. Declan Doyle's offense generated more than 500 yards in its first meaningful game. The Ravens didn't play their starters in the preseason, and many of these players are still learning the system. That's the scary part.

What happens when the operation becomes even more comfortable? Here's a theory. If Baltimore continues producing at this level, Doyle's name could start appearing on future head coaching candidate lists much sooner than expected.

Do the Ravens need help at wide receiver already?

This isn't panic. It's a question worth monitoring. After a fantastic showing, Zay Flowers left the game with a hamstring injury . Meanwhile, Ja'Kobi Lane exited the contest with a wrist injury and did not return .

Suddenly, what looked like a relatively thin group feels a little thinner. The Ravens have options, but they may need someone to step up quickly if either injury lingers, especially since there's something else about this corps worth noting.

Rashod Bateman remains one of the biggest unanswered questions

Bateman's lone catch was erased by a penalty. Remove that play, and he officially finished without a reception while drawing only one other target. It's far too early to overreact, especially considering Baltimore's offensive success. Still, for a player seeking a bounce-back season, this wasn't the start many envisioned.

The larger question is whether Week 1 was simply a product of circumstance or an early glimpse of Bateman's place in the pecking order. Derrick Henry touched the ball 23 times. Zay Flowers remained Lamar Jackson's most explosive weapon before leaving with an injury. The Ravens spread the football around to nine different receivers. Opportunities were always going to be limited.

Still, Bateman enters Week 2 as one of the roster's more intriguing storylines. If Flowers or Ja'Kobi Lane miss time, Baltimore may need him to assume a larger role sooner than expected.

Of course, that's the nature of Week 1. One game creates as many questions as it answers. The Ravens leave Indianapolis with a 1-0 record, a dominant offensive performance, and plenty of reasons to be optimistic. If these early impressions prove accurate, Baltimore may have left Lucas Oil Stadium with something even more valuable than a victory — evidence that this team could be every bit as dangerous as its lofty expectations suggest.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts: It's about meeting the moment when opportunity comes
articles.summary: There were some long stretches during Sunday's game when the Eagles offense failed to click, including five three-and-outs in 11 total possessions, but they...
articles.body:
There were some long stretches during Sunday's game when the Eagles offense failed to click, including five three-and-outs in 11 total possessions, but they were able to beat the Commanders because of big plays that got sprinkled throughout the contest.

Quarterback Jalen Hurts had a hand in many of them. He hit a 64-yard pass to wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks to set up tight end Dallas Goedert 's first touchdown catch and then hit Wicks for another score later in the first half. After the Commanders cut the Eagles' lead to one point in the fourth quarter, Hurts scrambled for 22 yards on third-and-18 and then hit Goedert for a 43-yard score that gave them the cushion they needed to finish out a 24-22 victory.

After the game, Hurts was asked about his ability to come up with big plays when his team needs them the most.

"Yeah, but it's not something that's forced," Hurts said, via a transcript from the team. "It's the same focus that you have throughout the whole entire game. It's the same poise that you play with throughout the whole entire game. And so, it goes back to all 11 being on the same page and then me taking responsibility and the opportunities I have with the ball in my hand. Talking about this on a production meeting leading up to the game with [Tom] Brady . When you're playing a position, a lot of it is about making sure you're in the right play, when you're doing the right thing that takes no talent. . . . It's just about meeting the moment when your opportunity comes. Collectively, we've got a lot to build on, obviously a lot to correct and I'm excited to get back into the process of becoming the team that we're supposed to become."

Putting together a steadier and more consistent offensive attack will be on the list of things to correct as the Eagles move into Week 2 and beyond, but that process will be made easier thanks to the knowledge that they can turn to Hurts and expect him to come up with something special in the biggest moments of games.

articles.title: Stock up, stock down following the Jets' win over the Titans
articles.summary: Here is the stock report for the New York Jets following Sunday's season-opening 23-10 win over Cam Ward and the Tennessee Titans.
articles.body:
The New York Jets (1-0) came into the 2026 NFL season with the hope that adding veterans like quarterback Geno Smith would help the team go down the road of being respectable. New York 's first test of the regular season came on Sunday as the Jets visited quarterback Cam Ward and the Tennessee Titans (0-1) and they were able to come out on top.

The Jets beat the Titans 23-10 on Sunday thanks to the offensive and defensive sides of the football working together in a way that fans did not see much of last season. Smith finished the game having completed 19 of his 24 passes for 215 yards while running back Breece Hall had a great start to the campaign with 22 carries with 102 yards and one touchdown.

On the other side, Ward struggled to get anything going thanks to New York's defense as he completed 19 of his 32 passes for just 140 yards and one touchdown that was scored in the fourth quarter. Both the Jets and Titans are rebuilding teams, but New York was able to emerge victorious.

With that, here is Jets Wire's stock report for the Jets following Sunday's win over Tennessee:

Even with the addition of Smith this offseason, Hall was going to be the player that the offense would need to set the tone if the Jets are going to a competent offense in most games. Not only did Hall run all over the Titans in this one, but he also caught both of his targets for 16 yards, once again showing his impact on the game in more ways than just running the football.

In a game where Smith completed a pass to eight different receivers over the course of this game, Taylor was the only one to not record positive yardage, showing how much he struggled to make an impact. With fellow tight end Kenyon Sadiq putting his athleticism on display in multiple ways, Taylor not being able to get anything going in this dominant win is nothing short of disappointing.

From the beginning of this contest, Bailey was making his presence along Tennessee's offensive line and in the backfield with the way that he was able to overpower whoever was blocking him in single coverage. Bailey, the No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, had plenty of draft capital invested in him and his debut should make every fan feel positive about what's to come for the rest of this season.

This entry is more to indicate that more should be expected out of someone like McDonald given the kind of havoc he can cause on any given Sunday thanks to his speed and athleticism. McDonald did get all the way to Ward and was able to bring him down to the ground for a sack, but outside of that, McDonald was unable to keep the pressure on like many expect from him in most games.

As touched on earlier, Sadiq made the quite the debut for the 21-year-old as he finished this game fourth on the team in receiving yards (21) and scored a rushing touchdown. Smith will need all of his receivers to get as open as possible given the Jets' struggles passing the ball last season, but if he can build on what he did against the Titans on Sunday, he'll be putting up more prolific games before the campaign is over.

From the onset of this game, it looked like Wilson and Smith had the kind of connection that should be able to carry the offense for the entire season, especially if the coverage isn't as tight. Wilson has long proven himself to be the best receiver that the Jets have had on the roster in quite some time, but if he can build on this performance, he should be on his way to having a career year.
